findings.title: Trace success and task identity are not independently verified
findings.affected_component: experience trace to procedure cluster boundary
attack_path: A producer records repeated structured traces with misleading success outcomes or task IDs.
The traces satisfy deterministic repetition thresholds.
The detector emits a suggestion backed by caller-asserted rather than execution-verified evidence.
evidence: ExperienceTraceCreate accepts caller-managed task_id, outcome, and significance.
Candidates remain suggested and have no promotion or execution command.
findings.recommendation: Require independently bound execution and evaluation receipts before a suggestion can enter procedural memory or skill validation.

findings.title: Repeated malicious metadata can manufacture a candidate
attack_path: A trace producer submits the same syntactically valid operation skeleton across distinct task IDs.
No matching non-success traces are supplied.
The repeated skeleton becomes a suggestion.
evidence: The detector validates structure, frequency, distinct tasks, significance, and conformance but cannot establish source honesty.
No candidate is written to memory or activated as a skill.
findings.recommendation: Keep suggestions authority-free and require source authentication, held-out reproduction, and negative tests before promotion.

findings.title: Operation skeletons can reveal procedural behavior
attack_path: A sensitive workflow is recorded as structured operation metadata.
A reader with database access learns the operation skeleton and supporting trace identifiers.
evidence: Raw parameter values and hashes are not retained in candidate rows.
Operation names, variability counts, and local trace IDs remain visible by design.
findings.recommendation: Do not capture proprietary or credential-bearing workflows without an approved scope and host-level database access controls.

findings.title: Structured sequence parsing is closed and resource bounded
attack_path: A trace contains oversized, nested, malformed, or ambiguous sequence metadata.
An unbounded parser could consume resources or accept unintended structures.
evidence: The source scan is capped at 500 traces.
Sequences allow 2-64 closed steps, 16 scalar parameters per step, bounded strings, and exactly one structured sequence per trace.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the closed schema and refuse source sets above the configured cap.

findings.title: A suggestion is insufficient evidence for skill promotion
attack_path: A future component treats suggested status as certification.
It converts the skeleton directly into executable instructions.
An unverified procedure gains tool authority.
evidence: The implemented CLI exposes detect and report only.
The detector never calls memory, skill generation, validation, activation, tools, shell, or network services.
findings.recommendation: Require explicit distillation, sandbox validation, benchmark, quarantine, and human promotion gates in any future bridge.

limitations: The review does not authenticate historical trace producers or independently reproduce claimed outcomes.
Exact structural clustering favors false negatives and is not a semantic similarity benchmark.
Host filesystem permissions govern access to raw traces and derived reports.
